data: Is the mean naive distance consistently higher for risk-assessed conversations than non-risk-assessed conversations?

The first graph shows the mean naive distance for risk-assessed (orange) and non-risk-assessed (black) conversations across different segments of the conversation. The orange line represents risk-assessed conversations, while the black line represents non-risk-assessed conversations. The y-axis represents the mean naive distance, and the x-axis represents the conversation segment.

From the graph, we can observe that the mean naive distance is consistently higher for risk-assessed conversations than non-risk-assessed conversations throughout the entire conversation segment. This is evident from the fact that the orange line (risk-assessed) is always above the black line (non-risk-assessed) on the graph. Therefore, the mean naive distance is indeed consistently higher for risk-assessed conversations than non-risk-assessed conversations.
